documents.title: 323 Instructional and Assignment Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no single stance; it gives each faculty member discretion ('individual faculty members have the discretion to set standards and procedures') while supplying a fallback ban when silent. Because the decision is handed to instructors, it is delegates.
documents.summary: Board-approved Provost policy on instructional and assignment AI use. Faculty set course standards; students may use GAI only as permitted and may not outsource work; AI is banned absent explicit standards. Also covers faculty and staff use, data privacy, verification and misconduct.

units.why: The purpose sentence frames the policy's aim: it covers student, faculty and staff AI use for 'instructional and/or assignment purposes', a statement of purpose and scope, so P56.
units.anchor: standards and procedures for student, faculty, and staff use of artificial intelligence

units.why: Users 'should do so in ways that are responsible, ethical, and consistent with university guidelines'; a principle of responsible use, which belongs with the institution-wide framework (P56) rather than a specific rule.
units.anchor: should do so in ways that are responsible, ethical, and consistent with university guidelines

units.why: The scope clause says the policy 'does not apply to the use of AI tools ... for research, in noninstructional settings, or for personal use', a scope definition, so P61.
units.anchor: does not apply to the use of AI tools, however defined, for research
units.fit_note: Also excludes research and personal use from the policy rather than governing them.

units.why: The definition of AI ('machine-based systems that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions') fixes what the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: a variety of a machine-based systems that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives

units.why: The definition of generative AI ('machine learning technologies capable of generating new content') sets the policy's object, so P61.
units.anchor: machine learning technologies capable of generating new content

units.why: Units are 'encouraged to provide broad guidance' on AI use; this recommends unit-level guidance rather than setting a rule, nearest P04, addressed to admin.
units.anchor: Colleges, departments, and other university units are encouraged to provide broad guidance
units.fit_note: Encourages unit-level guidance rather than per-instructor rules.

units.why: 'individual faculty members have the discretion to set standards and procedures' for GAI in their sections: the decision is delegated to each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: individual faculty members have the discretion to set standards and procedures

units.why: Standards 'should be carefully articulated in class and the syllabus': instructors are told to communicate AI expectations in the syllabus, P09 (should, not must).
units.anchor: should be carefully articulated in class and the syllabus
units.frag_start: These standards and procedures should address

units.why: Standards 'should address the limits of permissible GAI use (including attributing and/or citing GAI tools, if appropriate)'; this tells instructors what to cover, so P04 rather than P24, which is a student disclosure duty.
units.anchor: limits of permissible GAI use (including attributing and/or citing GAI tools, if appropriate)
units.frag_start: These standards and procedures should address
units.fit_note: Also says instructors' standards should cover attribution or citation where appropriate.

units.why: 'Students may use GAI tools when permitted by faculty-specified standards': AI use is allowed only where the instructor permits, with the instructor deciding, P04.
units.anchor: Students may use GAI tools when permitted by faculty-specified standards

units.why: Students 'must not outsource the work ... to GAI ... in a manner that circumvents the intended learning outcomes'; they may not have AI produce the work they submit, P19.
units.anchor: students must not outsource the work they are expected to complete
units.frag_start: students must not outsource the work
units.fit_note: The prohibition is qualified by circumventing the course's intended learning outcomes.

units.why: 'Students should not utilize content produced entirely by GAI ... unless specifically authorized': AI-produced submissions are barred absent authorization, P19.
units.anchor: Students should not utilize content produced entirely by GAI to complete course assignments
units.fit_note: Applies to content produced entirely by GAI, with an authorization exception.

units.why: 'It is the student's responsibility to adhere to the GAI standards and procedures for each course': students must follow each course's own rules, so P11 (rules per course) over P29.
units.anchor: responsibility to adhere to the GAI standards and procedures for each course
units.fit_note: Stresses the student's responsibility to follow each course's own rules.

units.why: 'students should consult with the faculty member ... prior to utilizing GAI tools' when uncertain: ask before using, P10.
units.anchor: students should consult with the faculty member leading the course prior to utilizing GAI tools

units.why: 'In the absence of explicit standards ... GAI tools may not be used for any purpose in any graded assignment': a fallback rule when the syllabus is silent, P06.
units.anchor: GAI tools may not be used for any purpose in any graded assignment

units.why: Permission 'must be granted or denied to all students in a particular course in an equitable manner': a rule on how instructors apply per-assignment permission equally, nearest P04; the equity requirement is not captured by it.
units.anchor: granted or denied to all students in a particular course in an equitable manner
units.frag_start: In such cases, permission must be
units.fit_note: Adds that permissions for unanticipated uses must be applied equitably to all students in the course.

units.why: Faculty and staff 'may use GAI tools to support instruction' if compliant with listed ethics, privacy and IP policies; a rule on instructor use of AI in teaching, P59.
units.anchor: Faculty and staff may use GAI tools to support instruction insofar as that use complies
units.fit_note: Conditions the permission on compliance with existing university policies.

units.why: GAI use 'must abide by the university's existing Information Technology policies' (Policies 910, 920); a duty to comply with existing university policy, P77.
units.anchor: must abide by the university's existing Information Technology policies
units.frag_start: Instructional and/or assignment use of GAI

units.why: Faculty 'may use GAI to supplement and/or refine their creative and academic work', a permission for instructor use in teaching, P59.
units.anchor: Faculty may use GAI to supplement and/or refine their creative and academic work

units.why: Faculty 'should not rely on content produced solely by GAI to create entire courses': a limit on instructor use. P48 concerns disclosing and reviewing AI-made materials, which this does not say, so P59.
units.anchor: faculty should not rely on content produced solely by GAI to create entire courses
units.fit_note: Limits reliance on AI for whole-course creation.

units.why: Everyone is 'prohibited from inputting confidential data ... into GAI tools that retain that data': a privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: prohibited from inputting confidential data
units.fit_note: The prohibition is limited to tools that retain the data in their training set.

units.why: 'Content created using GAI may be factually incorrect ... should confirm the validity': users must verify AI output, P31.
units.anchor: faculty, staff, and students should confirm the validity of AI-generated content

units.why: Student GAI use not allowed 'falls under the definition of academic misconduct' under Policy 312: unauthorized AI use is misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: falls under the definition of academic misconduct established in

units.why: Employee misuse is 'subject to disciplinary procedures applicable in their academic or work unit'; no type covers sanctions for faculty and staff, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: subject to disciplinary procedures applicable in their academic or work unit
units.uncovered_note: Faculty and staff who use GAI in disallowed ways face the disciplinary procedures of their unit.

documents.title: 312 Academic Misconduct
documents.stance_why: This is a general academic misconduct procedure, not an AI policy; its only AI content classes unauthorized AI use as plagiarism and sets no AI stance of its own, so delegates.
documents.summary: General academic misconduct procedure with one AI mention: plagiarism includes unauthorized use of AI software. The rest covers process, hearings and sanctions without AI-specific content.

units.why: Plagiarism 'also includes the unauthorized use of paraphrasing tools or text spinners and artificial intelligence software': unauthorized AI use is classed as plagiarism and so as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Plagiarism also includes the unauthorized use of paraphrasing tools
units.fit_note: Also covers paraphrasing tools and text spinners.

notes: A pending policy 980 Use of Artificial Intelligence (July 2026 redline .docx) exists but is not yet approved; not collected. No CS department policy found. Policy 312 coded only for its AI mention; the rest is generic misconduct procedure with no AI-specific content.
